Business Marketing B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies B2B Marketing: Definition + Strategies Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Nov 6, 2026 Discover B2B marketing, common B2B marketing channels, and how to build your strategy. Key takeaways Business-to-business (B2B) marketing is a type of marketing that businesses use when focusing on promoting goods and services to other businesses rather than to consumers, and it involves strategies such as B2B content marketing, social media marketing, and email marketing. B2B content marketing helps you rank in search engine results, which can increase your visibility with potential customers, and help build trust using various types of content, including explainer videos, educational content regarding industry trends, and customer testimonials. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. Afterward, if you want to build foundational marketing skills, consider enrolling in the Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate . It takes an average of six months to complete at a flexible pace and offers opportunities to learn digital marketing fundamentals, become familiar with spreadsheets, and develop skills in social media marketing, relationship management, and media planning. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. Explore other differences in the chart below: B2B B2C What it is Marketing to the decision makers at organizations Marketing to individual consumers Product examples Software, office equipment, and supplies, co-working spaces Food, clothing, electronic devices, books, media subscriptions Service examples Consulting and training, web or graphic design, product distribution, ad campaign management Tutoring, hair styling, health care, home cleaning, car repair Buying motives Logic: What’s the financial ROI of an investment? What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Key takeaways Business-to-business (B2B) marketing is a type of marketing that businesses use when focusing on promoting goods and services to other businesses rather than to consumers, and it involves strategies such as B2B content marketing, social media marketing, and email marketing. B2B content marketing helps you rank in search engine results, which can increase your visibility with potential customers, and help build trust using various types of content, including explainer videos, educational content regarding industry trends, and customer testimonials. You can build your B2B digital marketing strategy by identifying your brand positioning and how set your brand apart from its competition, describing your target buyers, building your brand voice, and selecting B2B marketing channels. B2B marketing means targeting decision-makers at organizations, typically based on logical motics such as return on investment. Read on to learn more about B2B marketing, including common strategies and how to develop a marketing plan for your business. Afterward, if you want to build foundational marketing skills, consider enrolling in the Google Digital Marketing & E-commerce Professional Certificate . It takes an average of six months to complete at a flexible pace and offers opportunities to learn digital marketing fundamentals, become familiar with spreadsheets, and develop skills in social media marketing, relationship management, and media planning. What is B2B marketing? Business-to-business, or B2B, marketing is the process of promoting products and services to other companies to help them improve their operations. It helps create demand and brand awareness. B2B companies often offer products and services such as software-as-a-service (SaaS), professional services, consulting, manufacturing, and wholesale products.Some B2B companies are large and also offer products directly to consumers. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. Explore other differences in the chart below: B2B B2C What it is Marketing to the decision makers at organizations Marketing to individual consumers Product examples Software, office equipment, and supplies, co-working spaces Food, clothing, electronic devices, books, media subscriptions Service examples Consulting and training, web or graphic design, product distribution, ad campaign management Tutoring, hair styling, health care, home cleaning, car repair Buying motives Logic: What’s the financial ROI of an investment? What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Sales cycle Longer sales cycle as decision makers consider the return on investment Shorter sales cycle, especially for impulse purchases Market research focus Firmographics of businesses and psychographics of decision makers Demographics and psychographics of individual consumers 7 common B2B digital marketing strategies B2B marketing strategies, which include B2B-focused content marketing, social media marketing, email marketing, and event marketing, can help connect buyers with products and services using a combination of data and content to achieve results. Discover some common B2B marketing channels , both digital and offline, as well as best practices for promoting your business on these channels to help plan your next steps. B2B content marketing Content marketing , particularly SEO content on your website , is an effective way to reach a target audience of B2B customers. Focused content can build trust with decision-makers, increase your website’s ranking in search engine results, and provide a basis for marketing efforts on other channels. Different types of content that work well for a B2B audience include the following: Thought leadership and educational content on important industry trends and strategies that your target B2B customers can use Videos explaining how your products and services can help B2B customers Webpages explaining your company’s method of prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, and what these efforts mean for your target B2B customer Customer testimonials Read more: How to Develop a Content Strategy: A Step-by-Step Guide B2B social media marketing To attract B2B customers on different social media platforms, adopt practices that are specific to a business-oriented audience, and leverage the power of videos for product demonstrations, tutorials, industry highlights, behind-the-scenes content, case studies, “about us” stories, and business-building strategies. Additional strategies to consider include the following: Tailor your posts to each platform. For example, you could repurpose long-form content into a Tweetable tip, an infographic for Instagram, and an excerpt for LinkedIn. Set up in-platform purchase and subscription options on social media. Algorithms may promote this content to more viewers, as it doesn’t lead users away from the platform. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. For example, Amazon, Meta, and Apple all blur the lines between the two and require both B2B and business-to-consumer (B2C) marketing. Other real-world examples of B2B companies include: Microsoft Salesforce Mailchimp When selling to other companies, remember that B2B marketing involves considerations and best practices that differ from those associated with marketing to individual consumers (B2C). For example, B2B customers generally look for products and services that will contribute to a healthier bottom line while avoiding investments with a low likelihood of a return. Considering that businesses may be responsible for payroll and other large business expenses, there may be more at stake for B2B than B2C customers, so when marketing, you’d want to bear this difference in mind. What’s the expertise level of a service provider? Emotions: Will this product solve a problem or fulfill a desire? Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. Partner with micro-influencers in your niche (users with 10,000 to 99,999 followers) to gain access to their loyal, targeted followers. B2B podcasting Podcasting can be a great way to reach B2B customers and provide them with informative content in audio format. By discussing topics that help businesses thrive, your podcast can establish you as a B2B thought leader. Topics might include: Leadership strategies Industry news and trends B2B customer success stories E-commerce best practices B2B email marketing Email marketing can be an effective way to build relationships with B2B customers and convert leads (potential customers or prospects) into buyers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help optimize email campaigns, drive increased personalization, and automate content generation directed to specific buyers. Additional email marketing strategies to consider include the following: To build your subscriber base, design a lead-capture landing page that addresses a top-of-mind problem or need for your target B2B customers and promises a solution in the form of a lead magnet, such as a downloadable report or a free video tutorial. Make sure your lead magnet actually provides the solution promised on the landing page and demonstrates how your company can help other businesses operate more smoothly. Divide your subscribers into smaller segments based on their roles within a decision-making unit, the kind of business, where they are in the customer journey, and other factors, so that you can tailor email marketing content accordingly. Include attention-grabbing words in your email subject lines, such as solutions to a problem or product offers, to encourage B2B email subscribers to click. Craft each email message to deliver value and lead subscribers to a purchase decision. Emails can expound upon social media and content marketing pieces, offer exclusive information, invite subscribers to complete a survey, shape future content, and announce new products. B2B event marketing Hosting, attending, and sponsoring events, either in person or online, can increase your brand’s exposure and generate qualified leads. Successful B2B events can take on many forms, including: Workshops, classes, and webinars on topics of interest to your target B2B customers Networking events, exhibitions, and trade shows, where you can build relationships with company decision-makers in your target market and introduce them to your products and services Professional conferences where your target B2B customers can learn new information and network with peers Parties, performances, dinners, and other social events to entertain target B2B customers and offer individualized or VIP experiences B2B marketing word-of-mouth and referrals Loyal and satisfied customers can be a great source of new leads, especially in B2B marketing. When a business recommends your product or service and can quantify a positive outcome, it carries authority. To encourage customers to make thoughtful referrals, you might offer referral bonuses or set up an affiliate program . Paid search Paid search, also known as pay-per-click (PPC) advertising, refers to a strategy that marketers use to leverage search engine results pages (SERPs). Ads typically appear at the top or bottom of a search engine results page (SERP), and when an internet user clicks on an ad, the advertiser pays a fee. This strategy can support your B2B efforts by targeting ads to businesses looking for a specific solution that you can provide. To succeed, you'll need compelling ad copy, strategic keywords (search queries B2B customers use to search the internet), and data-driven insights. Build your B2B digital marketing agency strategy A B2B marketing strategy can have a measurable impact on your business as you expand into new markets for your products and services. Follow the steps below to begin building your B2B marketing strategy, starting with positioning your brand to stand out amongst your competitors. Determine your brand’s positioning. Brand positioning is the combination of factors that differentiate your brand from competitors in the minds of your ideal customers. Clear brand positioning can help you build brand equity and, thus, make your B2B marketing efforts more effective. How will your B2B products and services help businesses succeed better than competitors’ offerings ? What associations, ideas, feelings, and concepts will your brand create in customers’ minds? What will they believe about your products and services? What factors will inspire loyalty in your customers? How to create a B2B marketing agency brand positioning statement Use answers to the above questions to craft a brand positioning statement: [B2B audience] will choose [product/service] to experience [benefits and outcomes], because [B2B audience’s beliefs]. Describe your buyer personas. Create a distinct and detailed buyer persona for each type of business you serve. Start by gathering firmographic data (how different organizations behave) on the kinds of businesses you want to target, as well as psychographic data (how individuals behave) on decision-making units within these businesses, using the prompts below to start. Firmographic data on businesses: How would you describe the industry your target business is a part of, including key players, trends, opportunities, and untapped markets? What kinds of products or services do your target businesses offer? What types of consumers do they serve? How many employees work at these businesses? What’s the average annual revenue? How are these organizations structured in terms of leadership, departments, teams, and individual contributors? Psychographic data on decision-makers: What is the role of each decision-maker within your target businesses, and how will they interact with you during the sales process? What motivates these decision-makers professionally? What inspires them to work in this industry? Develop a brand voice. Your brand’s voice is essential to connecting with customers, personalizing their experience with your B2B products and services, and inspiring their trust in your business solutions. The brand voice will shape how you craft every email, social media caption, video script, piece of long-form content, web copy, and more. When conducting B2B market research, collect insights into the language that company decision-makers use to describe their challenges and goals. Draw from customer language to develop a distinct, empathetic brand voice. Select your B2B marketing channels. While it’s a good practice to build a presence and create customer experiences on multiple channels, don’t feel pressured to be on every channel . Prioritize the channels where your target B2B customers are most likely to engage with your content. Create a seamless omnichannel customer journey to increase loyalty and retention rates. Make sure you tell your full brand story on every channel so that your target B2B customers fully understand your offerings, value proposition, what you stand for, and how to take action. Identify your B2B marketing tactics. Once you’ve selected your marketing channels, your next step is to identify the specific tactics you’ll use to reach your target B2B customers. Four examples of tactics to implement include the following: Offer a freemium service or a trial period so B2B customers can experience the impact of your offerings on their operations. Take an account-based marketing approach by networking with contacts at key business targets, building rapport with them, personalizing the communications, and encouraging sales. Use cause-based marketing to design products and campaigns in collaboration with charitable organizations, demonstrating your business's commitment to creating a better world. Create a more impactful, detailed customer journey for a longer sales cycle. You can do this by delivering content that supports buying decisions and emphasizes the outcomes and benefits your products offer. Best AI B2B Agencies in Australia (2026) | GTM Engine How it works Pricing Services Websites FAQ Book a call How it works Pricing Services Websites FAQ Book a call Home / Best AI B2B agencies in Australia Best AI B2B agencies in Australia (2026) Updated 25 October 2026 There is no single best AI B2B agency in Australia: the right one depends on whether you need pipeline or a system. These nine Australian agencies cover lead generation, outbound, SDR-as-a-service and AI GTM consulting, listed alphabetically, with every description taken from the company's own website. AI B2B agency is a loose label in 2026. In practice it covers four different businesses. Lead generation and appointment setting agencies now build and enrich their lists with AI. Outbound agencies run calling and email programmes at scale. SDR-as-a-service providers rent you a sales development function rather than a campaign. AI-enabled GTM consultancies design the stack and hand it to your own team to run. They are not interchangeable: the first three sell you pipeline, the fourth sells you a system. How this list was assembled. Every agency here has an Australian presence and a live website, and every description comes from that company's own site. No pricing, results, reviews or scores appear unless the company publishes them itself. There is no ranking. Entries run in alphabetical order. GTM Engine publishes this page and refers outbound enquiries to one of the nine entries, Aaxcello, under a commercial referral arrangement, so read that entry with the bias in mind. GTM Engine itself is no longer listed: it builds websites and does not run lead generation on its own account. Agencies we could not verify as Australian were dropped, including several that appear on other Australian roundups but turned out to be overseas businesses. The nine Aaxcello Sydney, NSW A B2B cold calling and appointment setting agency run by its co-founders. It builds the calling on top of cold email strategy, describes its callers as "trained, onshore, and experienced", and publishes two month-to-month packages: Foundations at $2,499 + GST a month and Growth at $4,999 + GST a month. Best for: Australian B2B teams that want onshore calling with email underneath it, weekly reporting and a published monthly price. Australia GTM Australia A go-to-market consultancy offering, in its own words, "senior, hands-on GTM leadership for B2B SaaS and AI founders". Work spans strategy, sales, marketing, customer success and revenue operations, plus a GTM engineering and AI practice that designs AI and automation into the client's own stack. Best for: founders who need the go-to-market model designed before they buy any outbound capacity. Forrest Contact Sydney, NSW An outsourced sales and customer engagement business operating since 2006, covering lead generation, appointment setting, customer engagement and inbound customer support across Australia, New Zealand and APAC. It states a "100% Australian-based team" and describes its work as "powered by real conversations, not automation". Best for: sustained phone campaigns where a local calling team matters more than an AI stack. Illicium Sydney, NSW Describes its offer as "Strategy, Data, People and Technology to reduce your HR burden and lower your customer acquisition costs". Services run from B2B lead generation and outsourced inside sales through research and data enrichment to sales consulting and fractional sales management. Best for: companies that want a broader sales outsourcing arrangement than lead generation alone. J2 Group Melbourne, VIC Calls itself "a fully managed outbound sales operating system", building and running outbound functions for clients. The offer includes Australian SDR talent, dedicated offshore SDR teams based in South Africa, field sales programmes and account-based marketing sequences. Best for: teams that want a managed SDR function and are open to an offshore cost base. Lead Express Scoresby, VIC A B2B lead generation agency covering appointment setting, telemarketing, data list services, marketing automation and digital lead strategies. It markets itself on a "100% Results, 0% Risk" guarantee and on guaranteed, qualified, sales-ready opportunities. Best for: multichannel campaigns that pair phone outreach with data cleansing and digital. Nousu Collective Sydney, NSW Sells "B2B multi channel outreach, cold calling, and appointment setting run by our in house Sydney team", and states plainly that there is no offshore outsourcing. Services include outsourced SDR, lead generation and list building, cold email, LinkedIn outreach and executive roundtables. Best for: buyers who want every touch made by an Australian team and are comfortable with a monthly engagement. Its stated mission is helping start-ups use large language models and prompt engineering for GTM. Best for: teams that want AI built into their own GTM stack rather than the selling outsourced. Telemarketing Professionals Sydney, NSW Describes itself as a lead generation and appointment setting specialist, operating since 2010 from a Sydney head office with Melbourne and Brisbane locations. It emphasises Australian callers and gives clients real-time reporting access to campaign activity. Best for: straightforward outbound calling programmes where visibility over call activity is the priority. How to choose between them Find out who actually makes the calls. Ask where the callers sit and which number they dial from. Australian prospects can tell, and in a market of a few hundred target accounts one bad call can close an account for years. Ask what the AI is doing. AI that builds and verifies a list is a very different risk from AI that writes and sends email with nobody reading it. Ask which steps a person still reviews before anything leaves the building. Look at where the risk sits in the pricing. Retainers, monthly packages, hourly rates, per-meeting fees and per-lead fees put risk in different places. A package buys a team and a process for a known price; per-outcome pricing moves risk to the agency, which prices it in. Know which one you are signing. Get the definition of a lead in writing. Agree the qualification criteria before you sign. Without them, the working definition drifts towards whatever is cheapest to produce. Check your deal size supports it. Divide your expected cost per qualified meeting by your average deal value and your win rate. If the arithmetic does not clear, changing agency will not fix it. Questions What is an AI B2B agency? An agency that uses AI for part of the go-to-market motion, most often list building, enrichment, account research and sequencing. The label covers lead generation agencies, outbound agencies, SDR-as-a-service providers and GTM consultancies, and those four sell quite different things. Do Australian B2B agencies use offshore callers? Some do and some do not, and both models appear on this list. Agencies that use Australian callers generally say so on their own homepage, so it is worth checking before you shortlist. How much does B2B lead generation cost in Australia? Retainers, monthly packages, hourly rates, per-meeting fees and per-lead fees are all in the market, and most agencies on this list quote after a scoping call rather than publishing rates. Which agency does GTM Engine recommend? Aaxcello, a Sydney cold calling and appointment setting agency, as disclosed above. The list itself is alphabetical and unranked, and every description comes from the company's own website. Can AI replace an SDR? Not for the conversation. AI is reliable for building and verifying lists, researching accounts and drafting sequences. Qualifying a prospect on a call is still a human job. **About Zipify**

This role is based at**Master of Code Global**and is dedicated to**Zipify**, a Shopify product company formed together with Smart Marketer.

Founded in 2016, Zipify develops high-impact Shopify apps that help merchants increase conversion, average order value, and overall revenue. Its products are used by more than 18,000 Shopify brands, including Dr. Squatch, TUSHY, Buffy, and Victoria Beckham.

Zipify’s flagship product, OneClickUpsell, has generated more than $1.2 billion in upsell revenue for merchants. The app helps e-commerce brands increase sales by presenting relevant upsell offers at key stages of the customer journey.

Today, Zipify is evolving beyond a traditional SaaS model. The company is combining its proven products with AI-powered capabilities and high-value e-commerce services to help Shopify merchants achieve measurable and sustainable growth.

**About the role**

We are building Zipify’s outbound sales development function from the ground up and seeking a high-performing Sales Development Representative to help shape and scale prospecting for our e-commerce SaaS products, primarily across the North American market.

This is an ownership-driven position for someone who understands ICP-based prospecting, builds AI-enabled workflows, and thrives in an agile, structured, and fast-paced environment with clear accountability for results. We are looking for a self-starter who takes initiative, challenges existing approaches, and continuously improves how outreach is researched, personalized, and executed.

**Required background and skills**

*   3+years of experience in sales development or a similar outbound role, including proven SDR experience in a product SaaS company.
*   Experience prospecting for **e-commerce software products** serving online merchants.
*   A verifiable track record of generating qualified outbound meetings and achieving targets, with clear examples of your contribution and results.

## Job Description

**Title:** Sales Development Representative - Digital Commerce

**Location:**United States

**Department:** Digital Commerce

**Job Description:**

Columbus is looking for a Sales Development Representative – Digital Commerce to play a key function in cultivating opportunities and assisting with the development of our sales pipeline. In this position, your primary mission is net new pipeline. You will find the accounts and contacts. You will source and enrich your own target list inside a defined ICP using Zoominfo, clay, LinkedIn Navigator and other similar tools to reach trigger events to make outreach land and run tested cadence to turn cold names into meetings. You will have a direct impact on the business as you partner with account executives to see opportunities result in sales. We are looking for someone who is self-motivated, can work independently as well as collaboratively and enjoys helping clients improve their business efficiencies through the use of technology and business software applications.

The SDR – Digital Commerce will work with the marketing team at Columbus, sales executives and subject matter experts to plan and execute business development activities. Activities will be both strategic and tactical with a strong focus on marketing response follow up, lead qualification and nurturing. This position will have a heavy focus on driving net new business and prospecting. Daily activities will involve targeting potential customers with a strong focus on phone-based activities.

Note: This is a remote opportunity and can be based from any location in the United States. #LI-Remote.

**Position Responsibilities**:

*   Conduct desk research on new business prospects and source relevant contact and company data

*   Conduct prospecting activity to include outbound calls, emails, LinkedIn outreach and attending networking and industry events to build a pipeline of sales qualified leads and meetings

*   Work with internal and partner marketing and sales teams to conduct co-marketing and co-business development initiatives

*   Maintain a library of sales collateral e.g. case studies and articles, to use in communication with prospects

*   Keep up to date with key trends and pain points within digital marketing and ecommerce

*   Conduct initial discovery calls to uncover pain points and identify potential Columbus services to address prospect pain points

*   Nurture and manage relationships with prospects to drive conversion through the sales funnel

*   Manage and keep the CRM system updated

*   Crete weekly and monthly reports for the Head of Sales

*   Qualify 8-10 confirmed meetings per month once ramped; Meetings are qualified as a time set up with Director-level or above contact in operations, digital, finance or IT at a target account lasting over 15 minutes. No shows and “badfit” meetings do not qualify.

**Skill Requirements & Experience**:

*   3+ years as and SDR/BDR in B2B tech or professional services; Digital Consultancy and/or previous experience selling DXP, CMS, Ecommerce, PIM and Experimentation solutions are a plus

*   Knowledge of technology products and services, understanding of lead data and CRM systems and experience building relationships and gain trust over the phone and by email with professionals at all levels.

*   Proven track record of successfully booking meetings with senior stakeholders, decision makers and C-suite contacts.

*   Experience conducting outbound prospects through calls, email, LinkedIn and other channels.

*   Ability to show results: reply rates, meetings booked and quota history

*   Ability to connect with prospects, excellent communication & interpersonal skills, technology and internet savvy.

*   Ability to learn software quickly, highly organized, self-directed business style, with strong ability to prioritize, interacts effectively with all levels of management and other employees.

*   High level of enthusiasm, a strong work ethic, and highly self-motivated.

*   Must be adaptable, professional, courteous, motivated and work well on their own or as a member of a team.

*   Ability to handle a fast-paced environment and challenging workload and strong written/verbal communication skills and presentation skills.

**Knowledge and Skill Requirements:**

*   Strong understanding of B2B sales processes, lead generation methodologies and sales funnel management

*   Strong written and oral communication skills required

*   Knowledge of Microsoft office software tools such as Word, Excel and Outlook required

*   Past experience working with/in sales and marketing systems, specifically Microsoft CRM and HubSpot desired

**Preferred Special Requirements:**

*   Experience within the digital commerce space, with an understanding of e-commerce solutions, industry trends, customer challenges, and how digital commerce technology supports business growth.

*   Experience with solution selling in consultative environment

*   Hands-on experience with outbound sales techniques

*   Experience with DXP and digital commerce services or software sales

**Full Time Benefits:**

*   Columbus offers a competitive benefits package to all full-time employees. This package includes Health, Life, Vision and Dental Insurance, Short- and Long-Term Disability, in addition to, paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 401(k).

**Bonus:**Yes

**THRIVE, GROW and SHAPE THE FUTURE**People always come first at Columbus. We’re a global digital consultancy with a local presence, helping businesses transform and thrive through technology, data, and human insight. Just as importantly, we’re a workplace where careers are nurtured and development is supported through clear, structured career paths.  
  
Our culture is built on trust, collaboration, curiosity, and a shared commitment to delivering customer success. Whether you're an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll find the freedom to explore ideas, challenge convention, and shape your own path.  
  
**Diversity and Inclusion are close to our hearts.**By joining our team, you will be part of a supportive network that values your voice, respects your ideas, and promotes a healthy work-life balance. Our average length of service in the UK is 8 years, as we are committed to cultivating an inclusive workplace culture that celebrates and supports career growth and advancement in becoming a Trusted Advisor. We provide equal opportunities for everyone, ensuring a level playing field for all candidates. We actively encourage applications from all backgrounds to apply for positions across our organisation, and in return, we will give you the tools and support to **Thrive** with us, **Grow** your Skillsets, and be empowered to **Shape the Future**.  
  
**The role of Sales Development Representative**If you’re already working as an SDR or BDR within Digital Commerce or eCommerce and are looking for your next step, this is an opportunity to build on that experience as part of our Digital Commerce team.  
  
You'll help create new business opportunities for our Digital Commerce team by:  
  

*   Identifying and engaging prospective customers through phone, email, LinkedIn and events.
*   Building relationships with senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
*   Conducting discovery conversations to understand business challenges and opportunities.
*   Working closely with sales and marketing teams to convert prospects into qualified opportunities.   
  

**Travel and Hybrid Working**We have an environment that gives you the flexibility to achieve an effective work-life balance for you and your family, whether you want to work from home or at one of our luxury Cubo offices around the UK.  
  
We continue to offer our customers onsite consultancy time if requested, so flexibility around travel and overnight stays is expected, depending on the project requirements. Onsite time is planned ahead of time, within 2-week blocks, so you know well in advance where you will be working.  
  
We encourage those in customer-facing roles to aim to come into the office at least once a month, and also team meetings and client meetings; however, you can work from Nottingham HQ or any Cubo office regularly if you prefer, whichever suits you.  
  
**About You (The Essentials)**
*   At least 1 year's experience as an SDR, BDR or similar new-business sales role within Digital Commerce, eCommerce or a closely related technology environment. 
*   Proven experience generating new business opportunities through outbound prospecting, including phone, email and LinkedIn.
*   Experience engaging and booking meetings with senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
*   Experience using CRM systems and prospecting tools such as LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
*   An understanding of the Digital Commerce/eCommerce landscape and the challenges businesses face.
*   Comfortable attending events, networking and representing a business externally.
*   Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle.  
  

**What we can offer**You will be a part of both a local and global team, where you not only share knowledge but also a laugh or two. We value our employees and leave room for flexibility so that you can enjoy a work-life balance.

Editor’s Picks E-commerce has become an indispensable part of global retail. Like many other industries, buying and selling goods has undergone a substantial transformation following the advent of the internet, and thanks to the ongoing digitalization of modern life, consumers all over the world now benefit from the perks of online transactions. As global internet access and adoption rapidly increase, with six billion internet users worldwide , the number of people making purchases online is ever-increasing. Worldwide e-commerce revenue is forecast to reach 3.89 trillion U.S. dollars in 2026, up from 3.67 trillion in 2025, and this figure is expected to reach new heights in the coming years. Among individual countries, the United States remains the largest e-commerce market , generating more revenue than its closest competitor, China. E-commerce market leaders Internet users can choose from various online platforms to browse, compare, and purchase items or services they need. While some websites specifically target B2B (business-to-business) clients, individual consumers are also presented with a vast number of digital possibilities. Taken together, marketplaces account for the largest combined share of how consumers purchase items online , ahead of any single channel such as search engines or online supermarkets. Amazon leads the global ranking of online marketplaces by GMV , ahead of Chinese platforms Pinduoduo, Douyin, Taobao, Tmall, and JD.com. The Seattle-based e-commerce giant, which offers e-retail, computing services, consumer electronics, and digital content, recorded global revenue of more than 716 billion U.S. dollars in 2025. Taobao is operated by the Alibaba Group, the leading online commerce provider in Asia, while Pinduoduo is the company behind the hugely successful Temu. Mobile boosts e-commerce traffic One of the most visible trends in the world of e-commerce is the unprecedented usage of mobile devices. In the third quarter of 2026, smartphones generated 74 percent of all retail website visits worldwide , which also accounted for the majority of online orders compared to desktops and tablets. As the adoption of mobile devices is progressing at a rapid pace, especially in regions that lack other digital infrastructure, mobile integration will continue to shape the shopping experience of the future. What do global digital shoppers have in common? While online shoppers differ greatly depending on their respective regions around the world, there are general indicators that help with understanding basic digital consumer behavior. Search engines have overtaken marketplaces as shoppers' leading starting point for product discovery , though marketplaces remain a close and well-established channel worldwide. Even though the online shopping experience is less interactive than the in-store one, online shoppers appreciate the ease and flexibility of e-commerce. In the Business-to-Consumer (B2C) sphere, fashion remains the top e-commerce vertical worldwide , closely followed by food and beverage, while consumer electronics continues to post strong sales too. When AI starts shopping for you E-commerce continues to attract new consumers, with convenience remaining the key driver for shoppers around the world to order online rather than visit a brick-and-mortar store. A newly published analysis on agentic commerce explores how AI agents are starting to shop on consumers' behalf, forcing retailers to rethink product discovery, trust, and checkout control as purchasing decisions shift away from human browsing. As this shift takes hold alongside continued growth in internet penetration across emerging markets, online retail is set to become an even more automated and efficient part of everyday commerce. **Company Description**  
  
**Job Description**  
  
**Hi.** We're OFX, a leading financial operations company providing businesses and accounting firms with real-time financial control and visibility to do business anywhere in the world. With an innovative platform and 24/7 human support, OFX automates and simplifies doing business across borders, reducing risk and eliminating routine operational tasks. Offering global business accounts, payments to 180 countries in 30+ currencies and currency risk management solutions to simplify global payments. OFX further enhances business operations by providing corporate cards with spend management, bill payments, vendor management, and integrations with popular accounting and HRIS software, to help achieve better business solutions so accounting firms and businesses thrive.   
  
 Headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices globally, in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore and Hong Kong. OFX has been a trusted innovator in global money movement for over 25 years.   
  
**Purpose of your role**  
  
 OFX is seeking a driven, results-oriented team player to join our expanding sales team. In this role, you will be responsible for hunting and qualifying leads to build sales opportunities for the team. You will be the first point of contact for potential clients and will effectively articulate OFX's value proposition and discuss how OFX's products and solutions provide an opportunity for better business money management, financial operations and spend control. This role is ideal for a new graduate, or a candidate new in their career, who has a strong business mindset and is looking to start or expand their career in Sales.   
  
 Sales Development Representatives who consistently exceed their targets will have the opportunity to explore a variety of exciting career growth prospects within our dynamic and growing organization.   
  
**What you do**  

*   Source new sales opportunities through outbound outreach, growing our top of sales funnel
*   Perform additional research on potential prospects that are provided by sales operations

# FINANCIAL SERVICES GUIDE

FINANCIAL SERVICES GUIDE 

> 29 OCTOBER 2026

# INTRODUCTION 

This Financial Services Guide is designed to assist you in deciding whether to use any of the financial services offered by Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited AFSL 234527 (ANZ). It provides you with an understanding of what to expect from your interactions with ANZ. 

The ANZ Group includes a number of companies that provide financial services. 

You should refer to the section headed “ANZ’s business interests and associations” for more information. 

# NOT INDEPENDENT 

ANZ cannot refer to itself as ‘independent’, ‘impartial’ or ‘unbiased’ in relation to personal advice it provides because: 

• ANZ is the issuer of some of the financial products it advises on; 

• ANZ advisers can only advise on products and services approved by ANZ (which includes products issued by ANZ); and 

• ANZ may receive remuneration from product issuers in respect of some products or services. 

2FINANCIAL SERVICES GUIDE (FSG) 

This guide contains information about: 

• Services and products provided by ANZ – it outlines the kinds of services and products ANZ is authorised to provide under its Australian Financial Services Licence as well as other services and products ANZ offers; 

• Remuneration received by ANZ and related persons – it outlines the remuneration ANZ, its staff and other related persons receive in connection with the financial services ANZ provides; and 

• ANZ’s Complaints Process – this describes how ANZ deals with any complaints you may have about its services or products as well as providing key contact details to communicate a complaint. 

You will typically receive an FSG when ANZ provides you with financial product advice or sells you a financial product. 

Some parts of the ANZ Group have their own FSG. You will typically receive their FSG when they provide you with financial product advice or sell you a financial product. 

3OTHER DOCUMENTS YOU MAY ALSO RECEIVE 

You may also receive other documents when ANZ provides services or products to you. 

• Statement of Advice (SoA) – This is a record of personal advice you receive as well as the information that advice was based on. 

You will receive an SoA when ANZ provides personal advice to you. You will not receive an SoA where the advice was provided during a telephone instruction given by you to ANZ to deal in a product listed on a market or where the product in question is a basic deposit product, a non-cash payment facility or a general insurance product. 

• Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) –This contains general information about the product including: 

• The terms and conditions for the product; 

• Any significant risks associated with holding the product; 

• Information about the cost of the product; and 

• Details of fees and charges the product provider receives for issuing the product. 

You may receive a PDS when ANZ issues you with a product, offers to issue a product to you, or recommends a product to you as part of personal advice. 

4CONTACTING US 

You can contact and find out more about ANZ in the following ways: 

By Mail: 

Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited 

ABN 11 005 357 522 

PO Box 537E 

MELBOURNE VIC 3001 

Telephone: 13 13 14 

TTY: 1300 366 255 

Internet:  anz.com 

5PRODUCTS AND SERVICES ANZ IS LICENSED TO PROVIDE 

ANZ holds an Australian Financial Services Licence (AFSL). Under this licence, ANZ deals in and provides advice and services in relation to the following products: 

BANKING 

• Basic deposit products 

• Term deposits 

• Electronic Banking facilities such as Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) 

PHONE AND INTERNET BANKING 

• Non-cash payment facilities such as direct debits and cheque facilities 

INSURANCE 

• General Insurance 

• Consumer Credit Insurance 

• Life Insurance 

INTERNATIONAL 

• Foreign currency accounts and foreign exchange contracts 

INVESTMENTS 

• Capital markets investment products 

• Custodial arrangements 

• Debentures 

• Derivatives 

• Managed funds 

• Market making for debt securities, derivatives and foreign exchange 

• Underwriting securities and interests in managed investment schemes 

• Securities 

6INVESTMENT SCHEMES 

• Miscellaneous financial investment products 

SUPERANNUATION 

• Employer-sponsored 

• Personal superannuation 

• Self-managed 

As well as products and services provided under this licence, ANZ is also authorised to provide the following: 

CONSUMER LENDING 

• Credit cards 

• Home loans, residential investment loans and equity loans 

• Personal loans 

• Personal overdrafts 

BUSINESS LENDING AND SERVICES 

• Business loans 

• Business overdrafts 

• Cash management services 

• Leasing and asset based finance 

• Trade services 

INVESTMENT LENDING 

• Commercial bill finance 

• Protected equity products 

• Margin loans 

MISCELLANEOUS FINANCIAL RISK PRODUCTS 

BANK DRAFTS AND BANK CHEQUES 

DOMESTIC AND INTERNATIONAL TELEGRAPHIC TRANSFERS. 

7ANZ MAY OFFER PRODUCTS OF OTHER ISSUERS 

Not all products offered by ANZ are issued by ANZ. 

ANZ generally acts on its own behalf when providing financial services that relate to the following products: 

• General Insurance 

• Consumer Credit Insurance 

• Life insurance 

• Investment and superannuation products 

• Miscellaneous financial risk products 

If you need to know the name of the issuer of a product that ANZ offers you, please refer to the Product Disclosure Statement or Statement of Advice (if you receive either of these) or ask your adviser. 

ANZ provides all other services and products on its own behalf. 

8ARRANGEMENTS WITH EXTERNAL SERVICE PROVIDERS 

ANZ may from time to time engage a third party to provide financial services on its behalf. Where that third party does not hold its own AFSL, it will provide the financial services as ANZ’s ‘authorised representative’. 

Authorised representatives can be either individuals or bodies corporate. 

ANZ may authorise a company or an individual to act as ANZ’s authorised representative in respect of the financial services they provide. For example, ANZ may authorise an external call centre and its staff to provide financial product advice or authorise external contractors to work in ANZ branches or call centres on a temporary basis. ANZ is responsible for the conduct of these authorised representatives when they act on behalf of ANZ. 

9BENEFITS ANZ MAY RECEIVE 

FEES AND CHARGES 

You may be charged fees for financial services or products that you receive from ANZ or other ANZ Group Members. 

OTHER BENEFITS 

In general, ANZ may receive benefits (including from other ANZ Group members) related to the following: 

• Insurance policies or referrals 

ANZ may receive commissions or other benefits from insurers for selling their insurance policies or successfully referring a customer to the insurer. 

These payments may take various forms including, a proportion of the first and/or subsequent years’ premium payments. 

Commission payments from insurers are generally received by ANZ on a monthly, quarterly or half-yearly basis. 

• Investment and superannuation products 

In certain limited circumstances, ANZ may also receive commission payments for selling investment and superannuation products, which can be made up of: 

- a percentage of the amount initially invested; or 

- a percentage of the ongoing value of the investment. 

Commission payments made by superannuation or investment companies are generally received by ANZ on a monthly, quarterly or half-yearly basis. 

• Securities, derivatives, foreign exchange products and warrants over managed investment schemes 

ANZ may: 

- buy and sell securities and warrants over managed investment schemes; 

- issue derivatives, foreign exchange products or warrants over interests in managed investment schemes; and 

10 - underwrite the issue of securities or interests in managed investment schemes. 

When ANZ provides financial services in respect of the above products, ANZ may benefit by receiving either of the following: 

- a margin representing the amount above which ANZ sourced or funded the product; or 

- a percentage of the value of the first instalment of the product plus an annual percentage of the value of the final instalment of the product. 

This may be paid quarterly, or on the issue and sale of various products. 

ANZ may arrange for the provision of execution, clearing and settlement services by third party brokers in relation to financial products trading through licensed financial markets. When ANZ provides these financial services, ANZ may benefit by receiving a proportion of the brokerage revenue and other fees associated with the service from the broker. Payment from the broker is generally received by ANZ on a monthly basis. However, this payment may also be made annually in arrears. 

• Miscellaneous financial risk products 

ANZ may receive a commission for selling miscellaneous financial risk products. Commission payments are generally received by ANZ on a monthly, quarterly or half yearly basis. 

You may request particulars of any remuneration, commission or benefits payable to ANZ in respect of a particular product or service. 

The amount paid to ANZ from third party product issuers or service providers will vary from time to time. 

All benefits to ANZ form part of ANZ’s overall earnings. 

If you receive personal advice, more detailed information about fees, commissions or other benefits payable to ANZ or your adviser will be contained in/or with your Statement of Advice. 

If you will not be receiving personal advice from ANZ, you may request more detailed information about fees, commissions or other benefits payable to ANZ within a reasonable time after receiving this FSG and before we provide you with any of the financial services referred to in this FSG. 

11 If any fees, commissions or other benefits payable to ANZ or your adviser affect the return payable to you under a product, further details will also be contained in the Product Disclosure Statement for the relevant product. 

# REMUNERATION OR OTHER BENEFITS RECEIVED BY ANZ GROUP STAFF 

All ANZ Group staff receive a salary. In addition to their salary, staff may also be eligible to receive an individual reward based on their overall role performance. Individual rewards may vary based on demonstration of ANZ Values (including acceptable behaviours), performance against a balanced scorecard of measures (incorporating Customer, Financial, Risk/Process, People), business unit/divisional performance and ANZ overall performance. Individual rewards are generally monetary and paid directly to eligible staff into the same account into which their salary is paid, or in some circumstances, into another account specified by the staff member. 

In certain circumstances, staff members may be eligible to receive non-monetary rewards, such as shares, discounts on financial services products and study assistance. 

You may request further information about what your adviser is eligible to receive. 

If you receive personal advice, more detailed information about fees, commissions or other benefits payable to ANZ or your adviser will be contained in/or with your Statement of Advice or disclosure document for the relevant product. 

12 BENEFITS FOR THOSE WHO REFER CUSTOMERS TO ANZ 

ANZ may pay parties including external parties and other ANZ Group members who refer customers to ANZ a commission or other benefit. This could be made up of a single one-off payment or benefit or calculated as a percentage of the total amount of sales generated by their referrals. 

# ANZ’S BUSINESS INTERESTS AND ASSOCIATIONS 

ANZ’s subsidiaries include: 

• ANZ Lenders Mortgage Insurance Pty Limited ABN 77 008 680 055. 

ANZ owns 25% of BPAY Pty Limited ABN 69 079 137 518. 

ANZ may receive commission or other payments from insurers when it is involved in the distribution of insurance products. These payments are set out below. 

QBE and Zurich: ANZ receives 20% of premiums for mortgage protection insurance distributed by ANZ and underwritten by QBE Insurance (Australia) Limited (ABN 78 003 191 035, AFSL 239 545) (QBE) and Zurich Financial Services Australia Limited (ABN 92 000 010 195, AFSL 232510) (Zurich). 

CGU: ANZ receives a commission for distributing car, home and landlord insurance products underwritten by Insurance Australia Limited (ABN 11 000 016 722, AFSL 227681) under the CGU brand (CGU). ANZ receives up to 12% of premiums paid to CGU for ANZ Car Insurance and up to 25% of premiums paid to CGU for ANZ Home and Landlord Insurance. Commission is for both new and renewed insurance. 

ANZ will also receive other benefits from CGU in respect of the sale of these products. These benefits include an annual marketing allowance, and ongoing payments in respect of product development. 

Zurich and Insignia: ANZ has entered into separate strategic alliance agreements with Zurich and Insignia Financial Ltd (ABN 49 100 103 722) (Insignia) and Australian Wealth Management Limited (ABN 53 111 116 511) 

13 (Insignia Financial Group). Under these agreements, Zurich and Insignia Financial Group will design, make available and issue specified ANZ-branded financial products and purchaser-branded financial products to ANZ customers in Australia. In Insignia Financial Group’s case, the ANZ branded products will be superannuation and investment products. 

Zurich will pay ANZ: commissions on the home loan protection insurance product of 20% of premiums plus an administration fee (payable per policy at inception); commissions on life insurance products, in accordance with the prescribed caps and claw-back requirements; grandfathered trail commissions on certain individual and group life products; and commissions on group life cover taken out by employers for employees (following a referral by ANZ to Zurich) at an agreed rate. 

ANZ also receives a commission of 20% of premiums for referring customers to Zurich who purchase Life insurance products provided by Zurich. 

Insignia Financial Group will pay ANZ: an annual fixed amount as contribution to ANZ’s forecast operational costs in relation to ANZ-branded superannuation products issued by Insignia Financial Group. 

14 A RECORD OF TELEPHONE ADVICE 

Where you instruct ANZ to order or transfer a product which is traded on a stock market on your behalf over the telephone, and ANZ provides you with advice relating to that instruction, you may request a record of that advice, unless ANZ has already provided you with one. 

You may request a copy of the Record of Advice relating to securities, derivatives or foreign exchange kept by ANZ. The request must be made within seven years of the provision of such advice and should be directed to your nominated representative. 

# PROVIDING INSTRUCTIONS TO ANZ 

You can contact ANZ by using the contact details set out at the front of this guide. Some products and services may have their own rules around how to provide instructions or carry out certain transactions. 

Please refer to the Product Disclosure Statement for your product for these details. 

# COMPENSATION ARRANGEMENTS 

ANZ has professional indemnity insurance arrangements in place to meet its obligations as the holder of an AFSL. 

ANZ’s insurance arrangements cover claims relating to the services and products it offers and the conduct of current and former ANZ staff (where ANZ is responsible for the conduct of the staff member at the time of the relevant conduct). 

15 MAKING A COMPLAINT 

If you have a complaint about any of our products or services, ANZ has established complaint resolution procedures set out below: 

STEP 1 CONTACT US 

Your first point of contact for raising concerns or providing feedback is our staff at your local ANZ Branch, Business Centre or our Call Centre. They will do their best to help resolve any issues you may have. 

• Use Locate Us on  anz.com  to find your nearest ANZ Branch or Business Centre 

• Call our Call Centre on 13 13 14 

STEP 2 COMPLAINT RESOLUTION CENTRE 

If you are unhappy with the response you have received or you would like to escalate the matter, you can contact our Complaint Resolution Centre. Our specialists will work closely with you to address your concern quickly and amicably. We will update you regularly until the matter is resolved. 

Contact details 

Call ANZ toll free on: 1800 805 154 (8am - 7pm AEST/ AEDT weekdays excluding national public holidays) 

Lodge online via:  anz.com 

Mail:  ANZ Complaint Resolution Centre 

Locked Bag 4050 

South Melbourne VIC 3205; 

Email:  yourfeedback@anz.com 

FURTHER HELP 

If you are not satisfied with the resolution offered by our Complaint Resolution Centre, you can have your complaint reviewed free of charge by the Australian Financial Complaints Authority, an external dispute resolution scheme. 

16 AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL COMPLAINTS AUTHORITY (AFCA) 

The Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) is designed to offer fair, independent and accessible dispute resolution for consumers who are unable to resolve complaints directly with their financial services provider. In most cases you have two years to submit a complaint to AFCA after you have raised it with us and received a final outcome from us. Before AFCA investigates your complaint, they will generally give us an opportunity to resolve or respond to it. 

Phone:  1800 931 678 

Mail:  Australian Financial Complaints Authority GPO Box 3, Melbourne VIC 3001 

Email:  info@afca.org.au 

Website:  www.afca.org.au 

AUSTRALIAN SECURITIES AND INVESTMENTS COMMISSION 

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission’s (ASIC) website contains information on complaining about companies and people and describes the types of complaints handled by ASIC. To obtain further information contact the ASIC Info line: 

Telephone:  1300 300 630 

Fax:  +61 3 5177 3999 

Email:  infoline@asic.gov.au 

Internet:  www.asic.gov.au
